An ardent Manchester United supporter, the Jamaican has also been a regular participant in the Soccer Aid charity matches over the past decade. Wythenshawe, who have yet to announce Bolt’s signing, have been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Uefa and Concacaf discuss joint Nations League in latest challenge to Fifa
Sports.content:
Uefa and Concacaf have begun talks about setting up a combined Nations League tournament featuring all 96 European and North and Central American and Caribbean countries, in another direct challenge to Fifa.

The Guardian has learned that having come together to push for Gianni Infantino’s removal in the light of the World Cup sell-off controversy, the two confederations are now working on creating their own biennial tournament, which could launch as early as 2028 after the next European Championship.

Although discussions are at an early stage, it is understood the new competition would mirror the current multi-league format used for the existing Nations Leagues by Europe’s governing body and Concacaf, the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football. It would be followed by a knockout phase, a final-four tournament to determine the champions.

League A would feature the top teams in Europe, including Spain, France, England and Germany, playing competitive league fixtures against the highest-ranked nations in Concacaf such as Mexico, the United States and Canada.

Uefa and Concacaf launched Nations League competitions in 2018, with the confederations staging fixtures in the same international windows, so the mechanics required to set up a joint tournament are already in place.

Under the draft plans the league phase would be played during the existing September, October and November international breaks, followed by knockout matches in March and finals in June.

As the fixtures would take place during international windows that have already been agreed, it is unclear whether the new tournament would need to be ratified by Fifa, although given the world governing body is in the midst of an existential crisis with Infantino facing a leadership challenge that may be a moot point.

With serious discussions having begun only in the past few weeks, the number of teams in each league has yet to be determined, but all 96 members of Uefa and Concacaf would be involved and much of the revenue pooled, generating significant additional income for smaller nations.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino is under pressure with Uefa and Concacaf pushing for his removal and now planning a combined Nations League tournament. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

The commercial appeal of the bigger European teams playing regular competitive matches in North America and Canada would be considerable, while there would also be major benefits for Mexico, whose football federation (FMF) is known to be frustrated by what it sees as the financial limitations of playing within Concacaf.

The FMF has held initial discussions about leaving to join the South American confederation, Conmebol, in a move that would need to be ratified by Fifa, but the prospect of lucrative matches against European opposition could lead to a change of heart.

The proposed new format would replace rather than add to existing international fixtures, while games would be played in geographical blocks to reduce travel.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) is also understood to have expressed interest in joining a global Nations League at a future date, and the competition structure being discussed would be flexible enough to accommodate them. The AFC does not currently operate a Nations League, however, so that would be a more long-term aspiration.

Uefa and Concacaf have been working together for some time, but have become even more closely aligned since the World Cup sell-off plan emerged last month.

Both confederations have made it abundantly clear that they regard Infantino’s position as untenable as a result of his role in the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, and are working together to propose an alternative candidate to stand against him in the presidential election next March.

Uefa declined to comment, although one source with knowledge of the proposal confirmed discussions are under way.

Concacaf declined to comment directly, but highlighted the confederation’s longstanding commitment to collaboration, which has led to guest teams participating in the Concacaf Gold Cup.

A historically strong relationship with Conmebol has resulted in many South American teams taking part in the Gold Cup, as have South Africa, South Korea, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

Sports.title: Two-time world champion boxer, 38, shot dead in deadly ambush outside his home with killers still at large
Sports.content:
Zolani Tete, a two-time world champion boxer, has been shot dead outside his home in South Africa.

The 38-year-old was killed in an apparent ambush in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape, at around 6:30pm on Friday night, officials confirmed.

Police said he had been arriving at his residence when he was approached by two unknown armed suspects wearing balaclavas while he was waiting for the gate to open.

The suspects, who are still at large, emerged from a vehicle and opened fire on Tete and a 27-year-old female passenger, who remains in hospital.

'He unfortunately succumbed to his injuries and was declared deceased on the scene,' police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana said.

'The female passenger sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was immediately rushed to a nearby hospital for medical treatment. She remains hospitalized.'

Boxer Zolani Tete was shot dead outside his home in Eastern Cape, South Africa

Tete was a two-time world champion, most notably holding the WBO bantamweight belt

Gantana revealed: 'In an attempt to escape the hail of bullets, the deceased drove his vehicle into the yard.

Tete most notably held the WBO bantamweight title from 2017 to 2019. He also holds a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a title fight after he knocked out Siboniso Gonya inside just 11 seconds in 2017.

Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture Gayton McKenzie said: 'South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced. Zolani "Last Born" Tete was shot and killed this evening in Mdantsane, at his own home, at the age of 38. A 27-year-old woman who was in the car with him was shot multiple times and is in hospital tonight. I wish her a full recovery, and I ask that her privacy and the family's be respected.

'I want to speak first to his family and to the people of Mdantsane. There are no words I can offer tonight that will be equal to what you have lost. Your son's name will not be treated lightly by this country, and my Department and I are at your disposal in the days ahead, in whatever way is useful to you.

'He was sitting at his own gate, waiting for it to open, and that is where they came for him. I will not speculate about who did this or why. That investigation belongs to the South African Police Service, and the detectives working it tonight need support.

'Two armed men in balaclavas got out of a car in Mdantsane and killed one of our greatest world champion at his own front gate, and they are still out there tonight. I appeal to anyone who saw anything, who knows anything, who heard anything, to come forward. Somebody in that community knows who did this.'

Tete last fought in London in July 2022, beating Jason Cunningham by knockout for his 30th professional win in 35 fights. But it was later ruled a no-contest after he failed a drugs test.

A year later, he was issued a four-year ban by the UK Anti-Doping Agency after testing positive for stanozolol. His ban ended on July 29 this year and after his death, manager Mla Tengimfene, confirmed he was training for a comeback fight on November 29.

Tete had not fought since 2022 but was training for a comeback after a drugs ban

Boxing South Africa said Tete 'inspired a generation of fighters' with his career

'It's been a tough and long journey and I am happy it's finally coming to an end,' Tete told The Ring earlier this year, still protesting his innocence over the adverse drug test finding, insisting: 'I don't accept the ban because I'm a clean and fair athlete.'

When asked if he was going to return to boxing, he said: 'Oh yes definitely, my plan is still unfinished,' he said. 'It's been a while since I stepped inside the ring, I am looking forward to my comeback fight and getting back to winning ways.'

News of his passing was met with an outpouring of tributes from across the boxing world, including a statement from the sport's governing body in South Africa.

It read: 'Boxing South Africa (BSA) has learnt with profound shock and sadness of the untimely passing of former IBF Junior Bantamweight and WBO Bantamweight World Champion, Zolani 'Last Born' Tete.

'The tragic incident reportedly occurred on the evening of Friday, 21 August 2026, in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape. Our thoughts and prayers are with the Tete family, his manager Mlandeli Tengimfene, the All-Winners Boxing Club, and Last-Born Boxing Promotions during this incredibly difficult time.

'Zolani Tete was more than a champion. He was an icon of South African boxing. A product of the famed All Winners Mdantsane boxing stable.

'He etched his name in history as one of the country's few two-weight world champions. His achievements in the ring from winning the IBF junior-bantamweight title in Japan in 2014 to claiming the WBO bantamweight crown, inspired a generation of fighters.

'His legacy includes holding the record for the fastest world title defence in boxing history, needing just 11 seconds to stop Siboniso Gonya in 2017 .

'We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, and the entire boxing fraternity. The sport has lost a true warrior and ambassador.

'Further details regarding official tributes and memorial arrangements will be shared upon engagement with the Tete family. We kindly request that the family's privacy be respected during this period of mourning.'

Sports.title: RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: Why the Saudis' swift and brutal termination of their LIV golf project coupled with the chaos and talent exodus at St James' Park should terrify Newcastle fans
Sports.content:
It's not ideal, right? An inexperienced manager, a squad stripped of its best players and Liverpool are first up. Those attached to Newcastle United would be forgiven some apprehension for where this fresh start might lead.

But that’s a tricky one to predict, because how far ahead do you want to look? Or framed differently, how far must you travel to understand the consequences for Saudi assets that don’t deliver?

One answer is particularly terrifying and timely and can be found across the Atlantic. Around the point that Newcastle and Liverpool finish up on Sunday evening, a golf tournament will also be winding down in Indianapolis. But not just a tournament – quite possibly an entire league, concept and dream, too.

And that’s because we’re talking about LIV and the distinct possibility of its death after the final putt is struck at Chatham Hills. After this weekend, the Saudis will sign no more of their cheques and an awful lot needs to happen for LIV to survive into 2027.

Why should this concern Newcastle? Well, that’s a conversation about their chairman, Yasir Al-Rumayyan, the high lord of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, and, specifically, the patience of those he represents when an investment gets too messy, too slow and too embarrassing.

We should head straight to the early part of 2026, when, according to multiple sources, Al-Rumayyan had offered a few assurances to the golfers of LIV. Their circus had been hemorrhaging cash, but he said they would be funded for years to come. As a golf obsessive, who once told the players that this league was his ‘f****** baby’, no one doubted the value of his word. Least of all LIV’s bombastic CEO Scott O’Neil.

Newcastle United go into the new season with an inexperienced manager in Matthias Jaissle at the helm

How long will Newcastle chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan play ball with the club if they are heading in the wrong direction?

Cameron Smith tees off at Chatham Hills in Indianapolis on Thursday, in what could be the last LIV golf event after the Saudis pulled the plug on funding

I remember having a long chat with O’Neil at the Masters in April, when he was giddy about LIV’s future. During all of this, a member of his staff thought he was being a little indiscreet with his predictions for Saudi-fueled growth, so he turned to me and said: ‘I won’t be put in a cage, I have to fly.’

Surreal as that may have been, it had nothing on what followed on the Monday after the tournament, when he was abruptly informed the money tap had been turned off. One point I subsequently revealed in Daily Mail Sport is that Al-Rumayyan didn’t even tell O’Neil directly – he had one of his henchmen do it. The baby was ditched on a doorstep.

Today, LIV is hobbling on broken legs. Vendors are suing for unpaid invoices, golfers like Jon Rahm are still due tens of millions from their contracts, and the season finale in Michigan was cancelled. Indianapolis was never meant to be the last stop for 2026, let alone forever, but unless promises from private equity groups shift into hard cash, it will be curtains for LIV.

Suffice to say, when the Saudis change priorities, it gets ugly and fast and emotion plays no part.

I don’t believe that is in Newcastle’s immediate future – a seat at the table in football is worth more than a sinking ship in golf, especially with a Saudi World Cup in 2034. Predominantly, the club has largely been a successful and useful investment.

But Saudi Arabian spending priorities have changed massively this year. And it ought to be noted, not downplayed, that earlier this summer there was an apparent willingness on the part of the PIF to sell a minority stake in Newcastle, ostensibly to lighten their own load on a stadium purchase that has dragged on interminably.

A new training ground, announced on Thursday, is a show of commitment, but a few bad boxes have been ticked of late. Messy, slow to progress and embarrassing? It’s been that kind of summer. The past two, actually, and that might be fine because the upside is worth riding a few storms. But here’s one – what about a relegation? For a kingdom appalled by the notion of losing face, that could be different.

Staring out at the new season, this all seems a touch pessimistic, perhaps. But it isn’t ludicrous.

Eddie Howe has left Newcastle and he was their difference-maker, their grown-up in the room, the leader who papered over cracks and delivered a trophy

Bruno Guimaraes has also jumped ship, leaving Newcastle to join champions Arsenal

That’s mainly because Eddie Howe has gone and he was their difference-maker, their grown-up in the room, the leader who papered over cracks and delivered a trophy. But his judgment, rarely doubted, also told him to get out of Dodge.

You don’t make that call if blue skies are overhead. No, you make those decisions when it’s exhaustingly grim and you know the unseen bits. You make that decision when you’re contemplating a sale of key personnel, such as Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali. You make that decision when Alexander Isak is long gone and Joelinton has indicated a desire to do the same.

You make that decision when those exits roll into a systematic failure to land the targets you truly wanted – guys like Hugo Ekitike last year and, more recently, Victor Munoz, who will possibly line up for Liverpool on Sunday.

The Newcastle inherited by Matthias Jaissle has been inviting a crisis for some time. Exceptional reporting by my colleague Craig Hope has exposed the dysfunction behind it all, from the boardroom down.

And so you do need to ask if the Saudis will embrace the chaos indefinitely. And you do have to wonder, persistently, if they knew what they were getting into, which is to say a landscape of ever-changing spending controls.

Of course, they don’t make violins small enough for big boys who can’t buy their way to glory. But if Newcastle could only finish 12th last season with Howe, what follows now that he and his best men are gone?

The bookmakers don’t think the worst-case scenario is so absurd – most of them have Newcastle at single-figure odds to go down. Viewed that way, those mock-ups of Kylian Mbappe in a black and white strip, paraded after the Saudi takeover, seem like ancient history.

No doubt Al-Rumayyan has offered some reassuring words behind the scenes. But there are a few golfers in Indianapolis who have heard a similar song before. For my money, those assurances would be worth about as much as a handful of plastic tees if Newcastle keep to their current trajectory.

The bookmakers don’t think relegation for Yoane Wissa and Newcastle is so absurd – most of them have the club at single-figure odds to go down

WHY FURY-AJ FIGHT WAS NEVER WEMBLEY-BOUND

Anthony Joshua’s fight with Tyson Fury, assuming it does indeed happen, will be in New York rather than the more logical options of the UK.

None of which is a surprise to Wembley insiders, who always suspected the promoters were grandstanding in their public desire for a bout on home soil.

My understanding is that there was a basic, belated act of lip-service to sound out the London mayor’s office in the past fortnight to discuss the feasibility of Wembley, with sources believing it was all a performative ruse to pressure Madison Square Garden into favourable terms.

The fight between Anthony Joshua (above) and Tyson Fury will be in New York rather than Wembley

EVEN MORE REASON FOR INFANTINO TO GO

It emerged this week that among other schemes, Gianni Infantino met with investors in the past year to discuss creating and commercialising an Under-15 World Cup.

When even kids are fair game, it really is time for a few adults to step up and drum this money-grabbing creature out of the sport.

RIDING PEP TIDES CANNOT HAVE BEEN EASY

Two thoughts on Amazon’s Pep Guardiola documentary and the astonishing outbursts of passion that it showcases so well. One is that it’s a pleasant surprise to see one of these productions deliver on the brief.

Two: we have marvelled at Guardiola’s genius for decades, but what about the patience of those riding his emotional waves each day? It can’t have been easy.

Sports.title: The real Roberto De Zerbi: Sources reveal how 'ruthless' and 'innovative' Spurs boss operates, the coffee machine anecdote that sums him up, the stories that show his softer side and how he's reuniting Tottenham with the help of club legends
Sports.content:
It is late in the evening of November 30, 2023, and Roberto De Zerbi is the only man sitting on the Brighton & Hove Albion team coach as it idles in the car park beneath the Agia Sophia Stadium, where his team have just beaten AEK Athens 1-0 in a group stage game in the Europa League.

De Zerbi has completed all his post-match duties. He has spoken to the media and he has addressed his players in the aftermath of the game. Now he has moved on. The rest of the Brighton party is still to board but De Zerbi is already on the bus with his laptop open and the glare of the screen lighting up his face in the darkness.

All who know him know that De Zerbi is a football obsessive and the game against AEK is gone for him now. He has started to prepare for the Premier League match against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge a few days later. Only when he feels he has done the work he needs to do does he pull his hoodie low down over his face and fall into a cocoon of sleep.

Much is made of the Tottenham Hotspur manager’s irascibility and combustibility but the boss whose presence at the helm of the team has led to predictions that Spurs will leave the travails of the last couple of seasons behind them has other defining characteristics that mark him out as a stellar talent.

Hard work is far from the least of those. He is also relentlessly demanding and intolerant of those who are reluctant to meet those demands.

Sometimes, that can manifest itself in a stream of complaints about faults he feels must be rectified. And that does not just apply to faults on the pitch. ‘A failure to meet expectation elicits a response,’ one former colleague remembers.

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi is relentlessly demanding and intolerant of those who are reluctant to meet those demands

But the Italian also has a softer side. ‘He takes time to check in on staff and their families,' a source tells Daily Mail Sport

Another former colleague at a club abroad remembers a time when De Zerbi grew irate because a coffee machine at the training ground had stopped working.

‘He wanted it fixed and he wanted it fixed now,’ the colleague says. ‘Not tomorrow. Now. He wants things to be right. He is a perfectionist in everything he does.’

Some felt, when he arrived at Spurs, that his impatience might create even more divisions at the club and that the egos of the players were already too fragile and too damaged to cope with his abrasive style. They pointed to the widely-shared footage of De Zerbi clashing with Marseille player Ismael Kone when he was coach of the French club.

De Zerbi was furious that Kone had held on to the ball for too long in a drill that was aimed at taking fewer touches and screamed at him. Kone began to walk off the training pitch. ‘Call your agent,’ De Zerbi yelled at him. The two men had to be separated before they came to blows.

That was not the only controversy De Zerbi courted at Marseille. He was resolute in his defence of Mason Greenwood, the former Manchester United forward, who was arrested in January 2022 and later charged with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

The charges were later dropped but it is unlikely that Greenwood, who now plays for Turkish side Fenerbahce, will ever play in England again. De Zerbi inherited him as a player at Marseille and said: ‘I regret what happened in his life because I know someone different from what's being described, especially in England.’

When he arrived at Spurs, aware of the backlash, he qualified his comments. ‘I have never wanted to downplay the issue of violence against women, or violence against anyone more broadly,’ De Zerbi said. ‘In my life, I've always stood up for those who are more vulnerable, more fragile.’

De Zerbi has already made a hugely positive impact at Spurs, starting with saving them from the approaching catastrophe of relegation from the Premier League last season and beginning to rebuild a sense of togetherness at the club that had been eroded by bad decisions and bad attitudes.

When he was Marseille manager De Zerbi was resolute in his defence of Mason Greenwood, the former Manchester United forward

De Zerbi's charm helped Spurs seal the £100m capture of Sandro Tonali from Newcastle

He refused to indulge the negativity that had consumed the club and which redoubled when Spurs lost their first game under his charge against Sunderland in April.

‘I saw the players after Sunderland in the dressing room,’ De Zerbi recalled. ‘I didn’t tell you in the press conference, but it was like this: all people crying, lying down on the floor in the dressing room. I said, “We pass away?” and I tried to transfer positivity.’

He spoke on the club’s pre-season tour to Australia of an evening at a Mayfair restaurant, Bacchanalia, he organised for players and staff near the end of last season when the prospect of the Championship was still beckoning. He spoke of the restorative benefits of a few glasses of wine on team morale.

His reputation and his charm undoubtedly helped Spurs seal the £100million close-season capture of Sandro Tonali from Newcastle United.

Tonali was one of the most coveted midfielders in the Premier League. There was no real reason why he should choose a club that finished 17th above other suitors. No real reason except the presence of De Zerbi.

Spurs have made other eye-catching purchases, too. Finally, there is a feeling of optimism about the team and a feeling that they have a manager who has the ability and the standing in the game to lead them back towards a place among the elite that their magnificent stadium deserves.

That sense of togetherness at a club renowned for factionalism was also underlined earlier this month when De Zerbi hosted a lunch at the club training ground for Spurs greats that included Steve Perryman, Glenn Hoddle, Chris Hughton, Clive Allen and Graham Roberts.

De Zerbi hosted a lunch at Tottenham's training ground for club greats that included Steve Perryman, Glenn Hoddle and Les Ferdinand

'He is intense but he is intense in a good way,’ says a source. ‘He sets high standards. He wants people to be the best they can be'

It was a good thing to do and it was the right thing to do but it was also a smart thing to do. When things are not going well, ex-players are often used as litmus paper by the media to reflect the mood. If their comments are not favourable, it can increase pressure on a club. It is much better to have them inside the tent.

De Zerbi made his reputation with Sassuolo and achieved two eighth-place finishes in Serie A with them before moving on to Shakhtar Donetsk and cementing his attacking, possession-based style that made a virtue of baiting the opponents’ press and drawing them out of position.

By the time he left Shakhtar in the summer of 2022 because of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, he was regarded as one of the brightest of young coaches. When news came through that Brighton had appointed him their manager, I was with Craig Bellamy, the now Wales boss. ‘Clever ba*****s,’ Bellamy said.

Like a lot of managers, De Zerbi likes to moan. He works hard to get everything he wants for his players. He works best when there is a buffer between him and the owner and if there is a worry about his tenure at Spurs, it is that there may be no one with the emotional intelligence to act as that go-between.

‘He is intense but he is intense in a good way,’ an executive who has worked with De Zerbi says. ‘He sets high standards. He wants people to be the best they can be and who are prepared to invest energy in the project.

‘He is intolerant of players who will not conform to what he wants. If you do not show the talent and the attitude he requires, he will cut you off.

'Maybe there is a popular perception that he bangs tables and shouts but he is a lot more subtle than that. He is a top coach: innovative, clever, highly-respected, ruthless.

‘He takes time to check in on staff and their families. When he was here, there was a member of staff whose son had just had an operation and Roberto often checked on his progress. He is surrounded by a coterie of Italians but they are all incredibly nice people. At Spurs, they will speak English when they are together, not Italian. They are inclusive.’

‘This guy,’ Pep Guardiola once announced about De Zerbi, ‘this guy is the No 1’

If there is optimism at Spurs this season after consecutive 17th-place finishes, it is because of the new boss and the signings he has made and the impact he has had, not just on the playing staff, but in the wider club. Spurs have secured the services of one of the best coaches in the world, a man supporters can put their faith in.

There is a story about the penultimate league game of the 2022-23 season after De Zerbi’s Brighton side had scored a late equaliser to draw 1-1 with Manchester City, who had already been crowned champions. For some time after the match, De Zerbi and Pep Guardiola sat alone in the home dressing room at the Amex, chatting.

It was an exchange that stressed their mutual admiration. ‘This guy,’ Guardiola announced to someone who walked in, ‘this guy is the No 1.’ If things had worked out differently, it might be De Zerbi in the hot seat at City now. Instead, Spurs got lucky.

Sports.title: Arsenal 3-0 Coventry: Premier League champions show their savage side as Christos Tzolis dazzles on dream debut, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
Opening night or an encore? There will be significantly tougher games ahead for Arsenal, but all indications from this one would suggest complacency will not be among any shortcomings in their defence of the title.

This was vicious and savage and effective in all the right ways. Had the Micky Quinn of 1993 been summoned by Coventry City, chances are he would have been dumped on his backside along with the rest of Frank Lampard’s men.

Naturally, there should be no rushes to judgment about what it all means, except to say that Mikel Arteta’s side kicked off this Premier League campaign by delivering on his two prime aims – a win and zero loose ends to offer comfort for those giving chase.

In the broad brushstrokes, the victory was secured with goals by Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard, but the detail is more important. For one, Christos Tzolis.

There are Norwich fans out there who might have seen a carthorse in their Greek winger all those years ago; Trojan horse might have been closer to the mark. Playing his first fixture in this division since 2022, Arsenal’s £33million signing from Brugge excelled here. Sure, he faded in the second half, but by then he had pummelled Coventry’s backline from his spot on the left.

In the broad brushstrokes, the victory was secured with goals by Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard

Arteta will have been left satisfied by his side's dominance on both flanks, as well as the performances of Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard

ad the Micky Quinn of 1993 been summoned by Coventry City, chances are he would have been dumped on his backside along with the rest of Frank Lampard ’s men

The relevance there is clear, because if he sustains that level, Arsenal will pose a major problem on both flanks. That will cause Arteta great satisfaction, and so too the performances of Saka and Martin Odegaard. One was a menace, the other a conductor, and together they performed different brands of torment on a team of giants. Ran rings around them, actually.

The perspective here is obvious – it was Coventry. It was at home. But it was also a party continued and one not dampened by the news earlier in the day that Bruno Guimaraes might miss a couple of weeks with a minor injury.

Prior to kick-off, there were fireworks in the sky, a brass band on the street and banners on each wall to remind visitors that champions reside at the Emirates Stadium. All of which might have been tolerable for Coventry were it not for the one-sided beating that followed.

For Lampard, this was a rough return to the big show. At the very least, he won’t be accused of discarding those who made the ascension possible. Or not immediately, anyway.

Of the 11 he chose for this first top-flight gig in quarter of a century, eight were part of the promotion campaign, with Caleb Yirenkyi, Loum Tchaouna and Aurele Amenda blended in from their £130million spree.

That was one point of consistency for Coventry. Another was their physicality – big lads got them up and big lads will try to keep them up, because no fewer than seven of Lampard’s side here measured in excess of 6ft and, lest we forget, he oversaw more goals from set-pieces than Arteta last season.

All of which meant there was momentary curiosity when Coventry won a corner inside 30 seconds. That it didn’t clear Riccardo Calafiori at the near post was a bad sign.

From there, they suffered something of a death by a thousand short passes. Arsenal were fast, ambitious and unpredictable, and through Tzolis and Saka they owned both wings. Tougher assignments are needed for a fuller judgment on Tzolis, but the manner with which he shredded Coventry’s right back Milan van Ewijk is promising for those who felt earlier versions of Arteta’s sides were lopsided.

It was, in fact, Tzolis who had Arsenal’s first chance, which he lifted over the bar after a rapid counter led by Saka and Odegaard. He was then involved in the second, spawned from a new short corner routine that favoured a ground strike over an aerial assault – Saka, Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelley worked to a clever script before Tzolis’s shot was blocked at the end of the move.

Playing his first fixture in this division since 2022, Arsenal’s £33m signing from Brugge starred

Prior to kick-off, there were fireworks in the sky, a brass band on the street and banners on each wall to remind visitors that champions reside at the Emirates Stadium

By this stage, we should add a detail – Odegaard, mostly stationed at No10, where we would also expect him to play once Guimaraes is fit, was conducting the music, just as he did in the Community Shield. With Declan Rice and Lewis-Skelly behind him in a 4-2-3-1, the unit danced around Coventry’s big men in the middle.

If there was a surprise, it is that the control only yielded two goals in the first half. The opener, converted by Havertz after quarter of an hour, traced to Tzolis winning his duel with Van Ewijk for a high ball, before Calafiori threaded a quick, low delivery to the German. Havertz’s finish would suggest an early upper hand in his mini-battle with Viktor Gyokeres for the striking spot.

The move for 2-0 came in the 23rd minute, when Rice and Odegaard led the surge and Carl Rushworth redirected Tzolis’s cross to the feet of Saka. He buried it.

Lampard made no changes at the break and nor were there any changes to the pattern of play. Arsenal continued to swarm, Coventry continued to grapple at thin air, and within minutes a two-goal lead was up to three. Again, it was conducted at speed, this time with Rice and Saka orchestrating the angles for a Ben White overlap before Odegaard scuffed the ugliest of finishes past Rushworth. The VAR investigated an offside against White but backed off pretty quickly.

A theme to note in that move was the innate understanding in space and movement between White and Saka – it has carried over from the title-winning season. So has the swagger. Arsenal are up and running.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi insists big-spending Tottenham are 'not finished yet' in transfer market and thanks board for 'keeping their word' on huge overhaul that could reach £400m
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi insists big-spending Tottenham are 'not finished yet' in transfer market and thanks board for 'keeping their word' on huge overhaul that could reach £400m

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed Tottenham’s board had been true to the promises made on recruitment as they closed in on a deal for Savinho from Manchester City worth up to £85million.

De Zerbi vowed Spurs were 'not finished yet' in the transfer market. A swoop for Omar Marmoush, also from City, is developing and they want Cody Gakpo from Liverpool.

If it all comes off it would mean a summer outlay close to £400m on nine new players and represents a radical change of policy for a club often criticised for failing to spend freely on players.

'I am very happy,' said De Zerbi ahead of his team’s Premier League opener at Brentford on Saturday. 'I can’t speak about the other coaches [before me]. I just can say, in my experience, they kept their word, kept what they said before I came at the end of March.

'But what we are doing is not for the coach. It’s for the club, for the fans, for the history of the club, for the pride of the club, and for the level of the club. This moment is crucial. We have to change the mood completely.'

De Zerbi claimed his seven games at the end of last season, escaping relegation by beating Everton on the final day was ‘maybe the best moment in football for me’.

Roberto De Zerbi thanked Tottenham's board for fulfilling their promise of backing him

He promised to set ambitious targets after two years of Spurs finishing 17th but could not set them yet.

'Now is not the right moment,' said De Zerbi. 'Now is the moment to think about Brentford, to complete the transfer market and then to follow the first two targets – to find the soul of the team and the style of play.

'Then we can fix what target you want without arrogance but also with big ambitions because this is Tottenham, not another smaller team.

'When we have finished in this transfer market, for a long time we don’t need many things and we can work all together in the right condition, in the right direction, to build step by step something special, or anyway to go to compete for the top of the table.

'Not maybe now. Or maybe yes, I don’t know. But we have the squad enough to play in every stadium in the right way.'

De Zerbi confirmed Micky van de Ven as his new captain with four vice-captains in order, Pedro Porro, Ben Davies, James Maddison and Archie Gray.

Van de Ven and Porro are not available for Brentford. Davies is unlikely to start and Maddison is not a certain starter after a minor preseason injury so 20-year-old Gray could lead Spurs out.

De Zerbi also said Lucas Bergvall, who told the club he wanted to leave earlier in the summer amid interest from Nottingham Forest and Newcastle, had changed his mind and was committed to staying.

'He wants to stay and we have no problem,' said the Spurs boss. 'He’s a top-potential player.'

Others could leave before the end of the month. Pape Matar Sarr is wanted by Galatasaray. Destiny Udogie has admirers in Italy and Spurs have an excess of left backs. Richarlison, with one year left on his contract, or Dominic Solanke are among others who could leave if Marmoush comes in to compete at centre forward.

Teenage winger Mikey Moore is expected to join Cologne on loan when wingers Savinho and Gakpo sign.

De Zerbi wants a competitive squad of 21 or 22 players and will not guarantee anyone a place in his team.

'I love speaking clearly,' said the 47-year-old Italian. 'Today is the August 21 and every one of those players knows the squad. If one of them doesn’t want to accept the competition inside the dressing room, they can leave.

'I try to be honest and take decisions to find the best first XI, but the players have to accept if we want to become better, to compete for the top of the table, 11 players are not enough, 15 players are not enough.

'If you analyse Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Juventus, Milan, there is a big competition inside the dressing room.'

Sports.title: Joe Root's second-coming as England Test captain starts with a bang at fortress Headingley - as dismal Pakistan made to pay by destructive hosts, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Joe Root's second-coming as England Test captain starts with a bang at fortress Headingley - as dismal Pakistan made to pay by destructive hosts, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

The dressing-room kettle had not yet been switched on for tea on the third day of this first Test when England were celebrating a crushing victory and a pristine start to the second coming of Joe Root.

Their bowling heroes, once more, were Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue, who backed up their five-fors on Wednesday with three more wickets each as Pakistan were dismissed for 135, to go with their first-innings 171. In all, they survived 85.4 overs, the equivalent of a less than a full day’s play. They were as dismal as England were destructive.

Robinson finished the match with eight for 80, and Tongue – who collected his three wickets in six balls after lunch – with eight for 89, both career-bests.

If Jofra Archer had started the rout by removing both openers, and finished it by persuading Mohammad Abbas to sky a slash to Dan Lawrence at backward point, it was these two, in their differing styles, who condemned the tourists to defeat by an innings and 103 runs.

For the first time in the game, the Leeds weather behaved itself – but while it never rained, for Pakistan it continued to pour. Robinson was all loping accuracy and both-ways menace, Tongue 10mph quicker and a nightmare to line up thanks to an action that goes beyond the perpendicular and obliges batsmen, especially right-handers, to play at balls better left alone.

When Archer and Gus Atkinson are back to their best, England will have a seam attack to conjure with, and there was an understandable spring in Root’s step as he encouraged Robinson and Tongue to lead the team off the field with a gentle shove in the back.

Man-of-the-match Ollie Robinson recorded career-best figures at Headingley

And Josh Tongue also returned his own career-best numbers and proved too hot to handle for the Pakistan batsmen all week

Robinson, by a sliver, won the match award, though no one would have complained if they had done to the medal what they did to the ball two days earlier and sawn it in half.

That followed meaningful runs for Jordan Cox and Lawrence, reinventing themselves at No 3 and No 6 as England reached an above-par 409, and an almost flawless display in the field.

And if there was any regret for Root as he discussed his first Test win as captain since seeing off India here five years ago, it was surely that Headingley is now off the rota until 2029.

This is not merely Root’s home ground, but England’s new spiritual home: a seventh win in succession was a national record. The Australians, who have lost their last two Tests here, must still be chortling at the thought they won’t have to visit the place next summer as they go in search of a first series win in England since 2001.

It is an act of self-harm the ECB may yet come to regret. ‘I’d love to play as many games here as possible,’ said Root, before diplomatically suggesting he should ‘stay in his lane’.

For now, though, there was simply relief at a job impeccably done, from the moment Robinson trapped Azan Awais with the game’s first ball. On a pitch which rewarded accurate bowling as much as it did judicious strokeplay, England were superior in all departments.

Pakistan’s awfulness made it difficult to draw wider conclusions. One suggestion that this is the worst team they have sent to these shores in 50 years has gone down badly in Lahore and Karachi, yet it’s hard to think of a rival for the tag.

Where once they would rise above their unfathomable internal politics by producing classy, stylish batsmen, reverse-swinging fast bowlers and world-class leg-spinners, they are now deficient in all three categories.

Only Abdullah Shafique, in the first innings, passed 50, while their military-medium seamers spurned helpful conditions on the second day. Mohammad Ali looks as hittable now as he did when he cost 5.5 an over on debut against England at Rawalpindi in December 2022. The fielding was a car crash. It was desperate stuff.

Jofra Archer launched a few lusty blows with the bat to take the game well out of Pakistan's reach...

Before claiming three wickets in the second innings to complete the rout

They have now lost 19 of their last 30 Tests, and need to avoid defeat next week at Lord’s to avoid tipping over into negative historical territory: after this game, they have lost as many Tests (153) as they have won.

Pakistan had begun their second innings 238 behind, but for the second time in the game lost a wicket before scoring a run, Imam-ul-Haq unable to sway out of the way of a brute from Archer which brushed the glove en route to Jamie Smith.

Archer then had Awais caught at leg slip for nine, a feather in Root’s tactical cap, though not the last: when Saud Shakeel worked Tongue uppishly behind square on the leg side, Root had positioned Lawrence there especially for the stroke.

Stephen Fleming, England’s incoming coach and a lover of unusual fields during his 80 Tests in charge of New Zealand, must have enjoyed that.

It was an excellent start to Joe Root's second tenure as England captain

In between, Robinson removed Shafique, the man likeliest to detain England, with a ball that squared him up and took the edge, and later benefited from two sharp catches at third slip by Cox.

Tongue had Shan Masood caught at first slip, then pinned Salman Agha leg-before. Later, asked whether Babar Azam might return from his hand injury in time for Thursday’s second Test, Agha replied with a smile: ‘I’m more than happy to hand the captaincy on to Babar Azam.’

For the first time in a while, the gallows humour was provided not by England, but by their opponents. Progress comes in all shapes and sizes.

Sports.title: Man United have got value for money this summer while rivals have splashed cash, insists Michael Carrick as they continue pursuit of Brighton's Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Man United have got value for money this summer while rivals have splashed cash, insists Michael Carrick as they continue pursuit of Brighton's Carlos Baleba

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United have got value for money in an inflated transfer market that has seen their rivals spending millions more on midfield stars this summer.

United have paid £50million for Andrey Santos and £35m for Youri Tielemans, and hope to complete their midfield rebuild after offering Brighton £65m for Carlos Baleba.

But the club were priced out of deals for Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes, who joined Manchester City and Tottenham for £116m and £85m respectively, while Newcastle have banked a total of £167.5m from Spurs and Arsenal for Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite concerns United have been gazumped by other Premier League clubs, Carrick is happy with his new signings and how much they cost.

‘There’s certainly players that have been more expensive, I think that’s pretty obvious,’ said the United boss ahead of Saturday's opening game at newly-promoted Hull City.

‘We’re delighted with the two that we’ve brought in, I think, and for the money of course. But actually, take that away, I’m delighted that we’ve got them.

Youri Tielemans came in for £35m from Aston Villa to bolster United's midfield

‘Certainly for the value that we feel we’ve got, I think we’ve done very well with those two especially. Two fantastic players give us really good balance, a lot within the team, and offer us different things.’

Rebuilding the midfield has been United’s main focus in this transfer window after Casemiro was allowed to leave as a free agent and Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious knee ligament injury at the World Cup that is expected to keep him out of action for much of this season.

As the club continue to pursue Baleba, Carrick added: ‘I think players have always come and gone through history here, and you’ve got to evolve. You’ve got to find ways of moving forward and ways of winning, essentially.

‘I know we’ve got a good midfield. We’ve brought in some really top players and really good characters, which is important.

‘We’re trying to improve the squad all the time. As it stands now, we’ve got some very good, top midfielders to choose from. So I think we’ve improved that.

‘You need a solid foundation through the middle of the team. I think if you look at all the great teams over the years, the spine is really strong. We’re conscious of that, and I think we’ve got a good spine of the team right now.’

United are still in the market for a left-back to provide cover for Luke Shaw, and Carrick does not expect anyone else to leave before the transfer deadline despite Joshua Zirkzee, in particular, being linked with a return to Italy.

Andrey Santos was a £50m capture from Chelsea, United's first signing of the summer

Asked if anyone has said they want to go, Carrick replied: ‘Not to me, no. I don’t know what’s going to come at us from elsewhere. We can control what we can control.

‘I’m really happy with the squad we've got so far, and if not, we want to improve it.’

Bruno Fernandes has also been the subject of fresh speculation over his future at Old Trafford, but United’s captain remains central to Carrick’s plans – even though he will have to protect the Portugal star after a long season followed by a World Cup.

‘I’ve said quite a lot about Bruno,’ added Carrick. ‘He’s been a big part of the team and the club over recent times and had a huge impact, so he’ll continue to do that.

‘In terms of the games, hopefully he stays fit and he’s in good shape. He’s a big player for us, he’s obviously our captain, but there’s still elements where we need to look after him.’

Sports.title: BBC axed iconic show, top star took pay cut, new Match of the Day pundits join in shake-up
Sports.content:
BBC axed iconic show, top star took pay cut, new Match of the Day pundits join in shake-up

The BBC has made a number of changes to its football coverage, including to its flagship programme, Match of the Day

View 2 Images It's all change at the BBC (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

The BBC has unveiled a massive shake-up of its football coverage ahead of the 2026/27 season, with a legendary programme getting the chop, fresh faces in the studio, and a lighter pay packet for one of the nation's favourite pundits.

‌



In the biggest headline of the broadcaster's new era, Football Focus has been axed after 52 years on our screens. The beloved lunchtime broadcast, which has been a Saturday ritual for generations of fans, is making way for The Football Interview, which is fronted by Kelly Somers.

‌



The changes behind the scenes have been just as dramatic. Newcastle legend Alan Shearer is staying put in his Match of the Day hot seat alongside Wayne Rooney, but official BBC figures reveal he is earning less for his services.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Match of the Day legend fears for iconic show in major warning to BBC bosses READ MORE :

How to watch every Premier League 2026/27 opening weekend game in the UK READ MORE :

Shearer's annual pay has dropped from his previous £440,000-£444,999 bracket down to between £390,000 and £394,999. It remains unclear whether the renowned pundit voluntarily accepted the reduction or was handed the cut, but despite the drop, he comfortably remains one of the corporation's highest-paid sports stars.

When Match of the Day's iconic theme tune kicks in this weekend, there will also be some new blood analysing the action. The Beeb has secured four fresh additions for the new campaign, with Ashley Young, Robbie Keane, Toby Alderweireld and former Tottenham and Brentford boss Thomas Frank all signing up for guest punditry duties as part of a revolving line-up.

‌



Eagle-eyed fans noticed that six familiar faces - Martin Keown, Dion Dublin, Shay Given, Stephen Warnock, Nedum Onuoha and Theo Walcott - were absent from the BBC's latest pundits list. However, Mirror Football understands the missing six have not been axed. All of them are still expected to play a role in the BBC's Match of the Day coverage this season as the broadcaster utilises its wider squad – just like any good team.

View 2 Images Alan Shearer remains a firm part of Match of the Day (Image: PA)

Looking to modernise their coverage, BBC Head of Sport Alex Kay-Jelski has promised to put supporters "firmly at the heart of the game."

‌



As part of the shake-up, the BBC is also making a major push into digital content, launching four brand new shows exclusively on the BBC Football YouTube channel: FANS², The Truth About Football, Golden Goal, and Football Hub.

These new formats will run alongside a fan collective featuring a supporter from every Premier League club, reflecting BBC Head of Sport Alex Kay-Jelski's promise to put fans "at the heart of the game" for the new season.

With huge names joining, a 52-year-old television institution making way for a new era, and plenty of fresh ideas, this Premier League season looks set to be just as much of a talking point in the studio as it is out on the pitch.

Sports.title: Fans the losers as Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury heads for New York
Sports.content:
Fans the losers as Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury heads for New York

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury have wasted their best years not fighting each other - now they are finally set to meet - but in New York, not London

View Image Tyson Fury is due to fight Anthony Joshua (Image: Tyson Fury/Instagram)

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury already come with plenty of baggage.

‌



In sporting terms, they are damaged goods. Six years ago Fury and Joshua held all four heavyweight world titles between them. The stage was set for a two-fight series to crown the division's first undisputed champion since Lennox Lewis. But Fury was instead forced to fight Deontay Wilder and Joshua lost his belts to Oleksandr Usyk.

‌



Now neither man holds a world title and both are on the brink of retirement. Now they will fight for little more than pride. But most fans have long accepted a clash between the British titans will not deliver what it once promised. They are willing to forget the past as long as both men put on a show.

‌



Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York READ MORE :

But they did at least expect that show to be staged in England. Ever since Carl Froch knocked out George Groves at Wembley over a decade ago, we have been spoiled for stadium fights. Joshua has headlined Wembley four times while Fury is no stranger to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Chris Eubank Jr and Conor Benn twice filled the Premier League ground last year. But those nights would have paled into insignificance when Fury and Joshua graced the Wembley turf. The idea they will instead finally trade blows in New York is preposterous. No matter how many times you say it, it will never make sense.

‌



The argument goes that Netflix, after initially agreeing to stage the fight in the UK, were suddenly spooked by an afternoon start time across the pond. But Joshua and Fury are no New York Knicks. They are not Taylor Swift. It would be a challenge to find a New Yorker who believes their city should be hosting the biggest fight in British boxing history.

A compromise of fighting in the wee small hours at Wembley proved to be little more than hot air. The Mayor of London was in support but never approached. It was New York or nothing. And if Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn had not dug their heels in, debate over the venue would by now be old news.

But even their resolve has weakened.Hearn now accepts a deal is there to be done and with the proposed November 20 date now just 13 weeks away, time is running out. Hearn will no doubt be compensated for ultimately relenting. Joshua and Fury will be laughing all the way to the bank.

Article continues below

But what about the British fans? There will be no reimbursement for a decade spent lining the pockets of their heroes. Even if every Madison Square Garden ticket goes to a visitor, 70,000 will still miss out. After years of frustration, some will say we should be grateful the fight is happening at all. But when the first bell rings 3,000 miles away, it will be a hollow victory indeed.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola makes transfer promise as Endrick responds to interest
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola makes transfer promise as Endrick responds to interest

Liverpool are primed for a very busy final week of the summer transfer window as Andoni Iraola prepares for his Premier League debut with the club at Newcastle

View 2 Images Real Madrid starlet Endrick has reportedly rejected a move to Liverpool (Image: David S. Bustamante/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Liverpool have a hectic weekend on their plate as they look to juggle transfer business with the small matter of their Premier League curtain-raiser. The Reds travel to St James' Park to face Newcastle on Sunday as Alexander Isak is reunited with his old club.

‌



Andoni Iraola has arrived at Anfield this summer under a wave of expectation. Arne Slot's second campaign on Merseyside was largely a failure despite qualifying for the Champions League and Iraola hopes to put the club back in the frame for title contention.

‌



More movement is likely required through the arrivals gate in order to make that a reality, however. Mirror Football has compiled the latest transfer headlines around the club ahead of Sunday's clash against the Magpies.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Endrick says no to Liverpool

Real Madrid forward Endrick has reportedly turned down interest from Liverpool to fight for his place under Jose Mourinho. The Brazilian is expected to be in for a battle for game time after returning to Madrid following a successful loan at Lyon.

Liverpool receive Brighton response after launching £50m Yankuba Minteh transfer bid READ MORE :

Endrick, 20, contributed eight goals and eight assists in 21 appearances in France last season. The forward hoped to return to Spain with new prospects to star for Los Blancos, only to see his chances dampened by the arrival of Yan Diomande.

‌



Vinicius Junior and Kylian Mbappe are automatic starters for Real and account for two of the three main attacking positions. That leaves £100million signing Diomande as the most likely name to fill out the remaining slot on the right.

Real also have winger Rodrygo, who is currently recovering from injury but is reported to be in Mourinho's plans. Yet despite that gauntlet of competition at the Bernabeu, ESPN has reported Endrick fancies his chances.

Sports.title: Footballer, 19, among four dead in horror crash as club pay tribute
Sports.content:
Footballer, 19, among four dead in horror crash as club pay tribute

Djedy Sidibe died when the car he was travelling in collided with a lorry on Monday August 17. Four young people aged between 18 and 21 died in the collision, while a fifth occupant was seriously injured

View 4 Images Djedy Sidibe died following the collision (Image: Jam Press)

A 19-year-old footballer is among four young people who were killed in a horror crash.

‌



Djedy Sidibe, who played amateur football for Zaragoza Galaxy, died when the car he was travelling in collided with a lorry on Monday morning August 17. Four young people aged between 18 and 21 died in the collision, while a fifth occupant was seriously injured.

‌



All five were travelling in the car, according to local media. The seriously injured passenger was flown by helicopter to hospital. A second car was also involved in the crash but nobody inside it was injured, while the lorry driver escaped unhurt.

‌



View 4 Images The group had gone to help at a YMCA summer camp. (Image: Jam Press)

Pilot dead after Pennsylvania State Police helicopter and small plane crash mid-air READ MORE :

The police are investigating the circumstances of the collision, which took place on the N-122 in Borja, Spain, as reported by NeedToKnow.

The five young people had been returning to Zaragoza after spending the weekend in Salduero, where they had gone to help at a YMCA summer camp.

‌



After reaching adulthood, several had decided to become volunteers with the organisation's Leadership Academy, helping younger people through the same programmes they had enjoyed during their own childhoods and teenage years.

Sidibe, who had Malian roots, was also studying for a Higher Degree in Chemistry and Environmental Health at IES Río Gállego. He played for Zaragoza Galaxy, an amateur team in the Major League Aragón.

His football club paid tribute to him on social media following news of his death.

‌



View 4 Images He was described as "a great person" by his club (Image: Jam Press)

"We at Zaragoza Galaxy are deeply saddened to announce the death of our player and friend, Djedy Sidibe, who passed away this Monday.

"Yesterday we received the tragic news of the road accident in which Djedy lost his life alongside three other people. The news has left us completely devastated and speechless."

‌



The club said Sidibe was much more than a footballer to those who knew him. They said: " "For us, Djedy was not just a player. He was a friend and, above all, a great person. Someone to share moments, laughter and happy memories with; one of those people who, through their personality, could always make you smile."

The club added: "Today, football takes a back seat. Today we say goodbye to a friend, a teammate and a person who will always have a place in our hearts.

View 4 Images The club is devastated by the news (Image: Jam Press)

‌



"We would like to express our deepest condolences and all our love to his family, friends and loved ones, as well as to the families of the other victims of this tragic accident. Rest in peace, Djedy."

Another of those killed was Saad Ahizoune, a young man of Moroccan origin who was studying for a teaching degree at the Faculty of Education at the University of Zaragoza.

The university also expressed its sorrow over the death of its student and offered its condolences. The tragedy has left relatives, friends, teammates and the organisations they were involved with in mourning.

The fifth young person who was travelling in the car remains in hospital in a serious condition.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard responds to cheeky dig from Sky Sports host - 'Thanks for reminding me'
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard responds to cheeky dig from Sky Sports host - 'Thanks for reminding me'

Martin Odegaard continued his fine start to the season and the Arsenal ace saw the funny side when he was reminded that he's already scored more goals than last season

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard was reminded that he only scored once last season - but saw the funny side (Image: Sky Sports)

Martin Odegaard was able to see the funny side after Sky Sports anchor Dave Jones reminded the Arsenal ace that he's already surpassed his goal tally from last season.

‌



The Norwegian scored the Gunners' third as they made light work of Coventry on Friday night. It is the team's second 3-0 win inside six days having also beat Manchester City in the Community Shield last Sunday by the same scoreline.

‌



Odegaard was also on target in Cardiff, meaning his two goals so far this season have outdone the one he scored last season. The Arsenal captain was made aware of that on Sky Sports, prompting him to respond: "Thanks for reminding me".

‌



Odegaard's strike in the second-half was a scuffed effort, but was still able to make it past Carl Rushworth in the Coventry goal. "Top finish I would say," he said sarcastically with a smile.

Last season the Norwegian's only goal came in a 2-1 win over Brighton at the Emirates, but on Friday he was named the Player of the Match as he excelled. Odegaard accepts that last season he struggled to replicate the level he's shown in previous years, but feels he's primed to find top gear once again.

‌



He said: "I think last season was a big struggle for me, lots of injuries and weird situations with bad luck. Could never find the rhythm, it is hard when you go in and out and sometimes you're maybe playing not at 100 per cent.

"It was hard, but I feel good now, my body is good. I had a good summer, a good World Cup and a good pre-season. Now I'm feeling 100 per cent and that always helps."

View 2 Images The Norwegian scored Arsenal's third against Coventry

‌



Arsenal's win was the perfect start to the defence of their title. Only three teams have ever gone back-to-back in the Premier League, but Odegaard insists that's the aim.

"For sure that's the mindset," he said. "We don't feel we have to defend anything. We want to do it again and that's the mindset. Last year is finished now, we want to do it again and we want to attack it and fight for it again.

"The perfect start. It's always good to start with a win. A win at home, three goals and a clean sheet. It was really solid."

Sports.title: Two-time boxing world champion shot dead aged 38 in fatal ambush
Sports.content:
Two-time boxing world champion shot dead aged 38 in fatal ambush

Boxing has been hit with some devastating news, as one former two-time world champion has been killed in truly horrendous circumstances

View 2 Images Zolani Tete has died aged 38 years old (Image: 2022 Getty Images)

Two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete has been shot dead. The 38-year-old was killed in an ambush outside his home in Eastern Cape, which is located in the south east of South Africa.

‌



Tete was known for winning the WBF Flyweight and WBO Bantamweight world titles as well as holding the Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout ever recorded in boxing (11 seconds vs Siboniso Gonya in 2017). He was expected to come back to the ring, having been absent since testing positive for the steroid stanozolol in July 2022.

‌



The 29-4 fighter had not fought since defeating British boxer Jason Cunningham in Wembley Arena in July 2022. Reports from his native South Africa broke the news about his death.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook pag

Eastern Cape police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana confirmed the boxer's death, while also stating a shooting incident had happened at around 6.30pm local time.

He said: "In an attempt to escape the hail of bullets, the deceased drove his vehicle into the yard. He unfortunately succumbed to his injuries and was declared deceased on the scene."

‌



It was also confirmed Tete was accompanied by a 27-year-old female, who was also shot in the melee, at the time of his death.

It's understood they had been waiting outside the gates of his residence in the Eastern Cape when two balaclava-clad suspects ambushed them and opened fire.

View 2 Images Zolani Tete's death was confirmed by Eastern Cape police (Image: 2022 Getty Images)

‌



The female who was with him at the time has been hospitalised with multiple gunshot wounds, according to Brigadier Gantana. He added: "The female passenger sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was immediately rushed to a nearby hospital for medical treatment.

"She remains hospitalised. At this stage, no arrests have been made...The suspects fled the scene and are yet to be apprehended. The scene is currently active. Our officers are attending to all necessary protocols. We are unable to confirm the identity of the deceased at the time.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Tete's four-year suspension, which was handed to him by the UK Anti-Doping Agency, expired in July. In January, he pledged to get back into the ring as soon as his ban was over, saying to The Ring: "It's been a tough and long journey and I am happy its finally coming to an end.

"In all the investigations my team and I were going through, we still can't really tell what exactly happened from our side.

"The closest answer we could get from Prof. Kintz was that it can only be a contamination, gathering the percentage of substance found and not being found on my toenails as they were tested by the Prof. Personally, I don't accept the ban because I'm a clean and fair athlete."

Article continues below

When asked if he was going to return to boxing, he said: "Oh yes definitely, my plan is still unfinished. It's been a while since I stepped inside the ring, I am looking forward to my comeback fight and getting back to winning ways."

Sports.title: Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'
Sports.content:
Man United set for transfer windfall thanks to sell-on clause as player in 'advanced talks'

Manchester United's transfer funds could receive a boost before the end of the summer window as they benefit from a deal agreed in 2024

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Man United transfer kitty could receive a boost (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to see their transfer funds boosted when Willy Kambwala finalises his departure from Villarreal. Kambwala, 21, is on course to join Italian side Como and United will cash in thanks to having the foresight to include a sell-on clause.

‌



Como are looking likely to pip Spanish club Osasuna to his signing and the Red Devils will pocket. United sources described the sell-on clause for Kambwala as "sizeable" when he departed the club two years ago after making his debut aged 19.

‌



However, Villarreal are only expected to take in a modest fee, limiting the amount that United will receive. Kambwala departed Old Trafford in 2024 when the Yellow Submarine came in for the player.

‌



Villarreal tabled an offer of €5.5million (£4.7m) plus €6m (£5.14m) in add-ons to acquire Kambwala from United. The agreement incorporated a buy-back option and matching rights for three years, alongside the sizeable sell-on clause.

United occasionally included clauses in player sales prior to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's investment in the club, but it has since become standard practice following Ineos taking charge of football operations It is now a crucial part of negotiations when players head out of the club.

United included a "high percentage" sell-on clause and buyback option in the sale of Tyler Fredricson to Lausanne-Sport, with comparable clauses also written into the sale of Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough.

‌



United inserted a buy-back clause into the deal with Boro, along with matching rights and a sell-on clause of up to 35 per cent to profit from any potential future sale. Ethan Williams was transferred to Peterborough last week, with United inserting a 50 per cent sell-on clause into the agreement, alongside a buyback option and matching rights clauses.

Ethan Ennis completed a permanent switch to Stockport County earlier this week. United included a 50 per cent sell-on clause in that deal, as well as buyback and matching rights clauses.

View 2 Images Willy Kambwala left Manchester United in 2024 (Image: Getty)

‌

"I just think we're looking to strengthen the squad," he said. "We're certainly working towards that, making the most of the situation that we have and trying to improve things and trying to move forward.

Sports.title: Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler responds to Man Utd's bid for Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler responds to Man Utd's bid for Carlos Baleba

Manchester United have submitted an offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba, who will sit out of their Premier League opener this weekend

View 3 Images Fabian Hurzeler spoke about transfer rumours involving his players (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler refused to be drawn on Manchester United's interest in midfielder Carlos Baleba on the eve of their Premier League campaign.

‌



United have submitted an offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons for the 22-year-old, who Michael Carrick wants to further bolster his midfield alongside new arrivals Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

‌



Baleba is keen on a move to Old Trafford and has reportedly already agreed personal terms. United first enquired about the Cameroon international last summer and are now confident they can wrap up a deal for considerably less than the £100m they were quoted 12 months ago.

‌



Hurzeler faced reporters on Friday ahead of Brighton's Premier League opener against Aston Villa on Sunday and didn't give much away, bar confirming Baleba would miss the game due to an ankle injury picked up in pre-season.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"He's a Brighton player. Like I said, I'll never comment on any rumours that are currently in the media, it's also something I definitely can't control," the German said.

"A lot of things are written, I know about situations but again, in two days I have a very important game together with my team and with my staff. We want to have a good start in the Premier League season, that's the only focus we have at the moment."

His words echoed those of Brighton chief executive Paul Barber the day before. "It’s not something that I can talk about right now," Barber told talkSPORT on Thursday.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester United are confident of signing Carlos Baleba (Image: Getty Images)

"This time of year we’re always going to be subject to bids for our players, we’re always going to be interested in ones that are sensible and are going to make sense for us financially, economically. But we also have to balance that with making sure our squad is as strong as it can be to compete in competitions like the one we’re in.

"So nothing really to say on Carlos at the moment other than that he’s a hugely talented young midfielder who’s done really well for us and has attracted interest from some of the biggest clubs in the world now for a couple of years."

‌



Brighton are also fielding interest from Liverpool in winger Yankuba Minteh. The Seagulls have rejected a £50m bid from Andoni Iraola's side and know the transfer game better than most, having lost many key players to Premier League rivals in recent years.

View 3 Images Yankuba Minteh is wanted by Liverpool (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

"We know in general all the players there are rumours about, they are important players for us because they're a big part of the journey the last two years," Hurzeler said.

‌



"In football, you have to understand, it's normal if you're successful as a team, if the team is doing well, they've had some good achievements, then an individual can shine. Then of course there will be a big ask for our players, that's part of our identity and part of my job here.

"It was clear for everyone this might happen during a busy transfer window. We can go through every individual player, we all know how important these kinds of players are for me, but we also know that good achievements, big achievements, especially in the Premier League, you create offers, you create a lot of attention."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
